correctness.rationale: The canonical divisor formula differs from the uniform coefficient sum by a Cartier coordinate-divisor contribution. Modulo that Cartier class, Cartierness of \(mK\) is equivalent to an integer cocircuit-weight equation with sum \(-2m\). In \(U_{r,n}\), all cocircuits have size \(k=n-r+1\); comparing k-subsets differing in one element forces every weight equal. Thus \(k\mid 2m\), and the least positive m is \(k/\gcd(k,2)\). The rank-one case is handled separately by its single cocircuit and the smooth curve \(Y_V\cong\mathbb P^1\).

An exact formula and an unbounded family among the basic uniform matroids give a useful baseline for comparing more complicated matroid Schubert varieties and show that Q-Gorensteinness imposes no uniform index bound in this family.
